overview: Server-side anticheats treat the entity-effect packet as state synchronization, not a cheat signal. The corpus splits into packet-driven potion trackers (Grim, Artemis, BetterAnticheat, Kauri, Intave) that decode S1D and mirror the effect onto their simulated player or entity, and Bukkit-polling checks (FlopAC, Hydro, Frequency) that read getActivePotionEffects and only see the effect after the server applies it. The trackers matter because movement checks must know the exact speed, jump and slowness multipliers the client has; a potion state mismatch causes false flags in speed and flight checks, so the apply packet is transaction-confirmed before the effect lands in the simulation.

checks.name: Effect state replication (Grim)
checks.purpose: Keep the compensated entity's potion state in sync with the server so movement predictions apply the same speed, jump and slowness multipliers the client sees.
checks.how_it_works: PacketEntityReplication listens on the packet-send side. For ENTITY_EFFECT it decodes the potion type and amplifier, cancels the packet when ViaVersion would fake an effect the client version does not support, forces a transaction when the effect targets the player, and schedules entity.addPotionEffect on the compensated entity at the transaction's real-time position. The remove branch in the same listener mirrors this with entity.removePotionEffect.
checks.detects: No cheat directly. It is state replication: speed, jump boost and levitation modifiers on the simulated entity must match the client's, or flight and speed checks misjudge legitimate motion.
checks.variations: Artemis (PotionPreProcessor, EmulatorPreProcessor) and BetterAnticheat (PotionTracker) use the same transaction-confirmed pattern; Kauri's PotionHandler adds the effect into a thread-safe list; Intave decodes the fields with EntityEffectReader.

checks.name: Potion preprocessor (Artemis)
checks.purpose: Maintain the user's active effect list from the entity-effect packet so checks and the emulator can read current potion modifiers.
checks.how_it_works: fastHandle matches GPacketPlayServerEntityEffect, builds a PotionEffect from the effect id, duration and amplifier, then queues the add behind a transaction confirmation: pre() inserts the effect and marks it processed, post() clears the marker. It also clears the using-item flag when the effect ends item use.
checks.detects: Nothing directly; it feeds checks that must distinguish potion-boosted motion from cheat motion.
checks.variations: The same anticheat's EmulatorPreProcessor applies the identical pattern to the emulated entity; Grim and BetterAnticheat use equivalent confirmations.

checks.name: Potion tracker (BetterAnticheat)
checks.purpose: Track each potion type's amplifier and duration as a lag-compensated many-state so checks read the effect that actually reached the client.
checks.how_it_works: PotionTracker subscribes to ENTITY_EFFECT on the send side, takes a confirmation handle, and stages the new Potion in an ObjectManyState: addNew on begin, flushOld plus an active-count after the client confirms. REMOVE_ENTITY_EFFECT stages an EMPTY_POTION the same way so an expired effect cannot linger.
checks.detects: Nothing by itself; getPotion() exposes the confirmed state to checks that need the speed or jump modifier.
checks.variations: Grim and Artemis use transaction confirmations rather than a confirmation tracker; FlopAC polls Bukkit's getActivePotionEffects instead of reading the packet.

checks.name: Potion handler (Kauri)
checks.purpose: Keep a thread-safe potion effect list on the player data so movement and velocity checks can query current modifiers.
checks.how_it_works: PotionHandler seeds the list from the Bukkit player's active effects at construction, then onPotionEffect(WrapperPlayServerEntityEffect) replaces the entry for the potion type under a write lock, storing the amplifier, duration and visibility flags. hasPotionEffect and getEffectByType expose the state to checks.
checks.detects: Nothing directly; the handler is the query surface for checks that must subtract potion-boosted motion from the allowed envelope.
checks.variations: Artemis and Grim decode the packet into their own effect model; Tecnio whitelists both effect packets in NetworkFilter and tracks potion levels in AttributeTracker.

checks.name: Entity effect reader (Intave)
checks.purpose: Extract effect type, amplifier and duration from the entity-effect packet across every supported protocol version.
checks.how_it_works: EntityEffectReader is registered for the ENTITY_EFFECT packet in PacketReaders. effectType() reads the potion-type field on 1.19+, the integer slot on 1.18.2, and the legacy byte below; effectAmplifier() and effectDuration() shift their field indexes at 1.21. Each accessor falls back to 0 on a missing field.
checks.detects: Nothing by itself; the reader feeds the effect tracker that movement characteristics consume.
checks.variations: Grim and Artemis read the same fields through PacketEvents and the cc.ghast wrapper tree instead of ProtocolLib.
